ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Athletic resting rhythm

A 24-year-old endurance runner attends a routine examination. His pulse is 44/min, blood pressure is 118/70 mm Hg, and he denies dizziness or exercise intolerance. ECG shows upright P waves before every narrow QRS with a constant PR interval. What is the most appropriate initial interpretation?

  1. Physiologic sinus bradycardia
  2. Complete atrioventricular block
  3. Atrial fibrillation with slow response
  4. Junctional escape rhythm
  5. Sinus arrest
Answer and explanation

Physiologic sinus bradycardia

Training-associated vagal tone can produce an asymptomatic slow sinus rhythm.

Option explanations

Physiologic sinus bradycardia: Training-associated vagal tone can produce an asymptomatic slow sinus rhythm.

Complete atrioventricular block: Complete block produces atrioventricular dissociation.

Atrial fibrillation with slow response: Atrial fibrillation lacks consistent sinus P waves.

Junctional escape rhythm: Junctional escape usually has absent or retrograde P waves.

Sinus arrest: Sinus arrest produces pauses rather than continuous regular sinus activation.
